title: How can we reach the alternate angle in two moves?
description: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal, and one angle is given as one hundred and twenty degrees. The board goes from that angle to its corresponding angle, and then to the angle vertically opposite that one. Keeko doubts the answer, because Keeko takes the two angles to be a linear pair.
teaching_notes: One idea: two moves, corresponding and then vertically opposite, and neither move changes the size, so alternate angles are equal. Watch for students who subtract the angle from one hundred and eighty, as for a linear pair.

source: Lines l and m are parallel and t is a transversal. The angle
video_script.why: The child knows corresponding and vertically opposite angles and chains them to reach the alternate angle, and sees that alternate angles are equal.
video_script.substitution: the book's own figure: parallel lines l and m, transversal t, eight angles a to h, f is one hundred and twenty degrees
video_script.anchor: parallel lines l and m cut by the transversal t, with eight angles a to h, and f marked 120°
video_script.wrong_move: subtracts f from 180 as if d and f were a linear pair
video_script.payoff_line: Each move keeps the size the same

final_answer.value: d = 120°, so alternate angles of parallel lines are equal
final_answer.spoken: d is one hundred and twenty degrees, so alternate angles of parallel lines are equal

maths_rules: b is the corresponding angle of f, so b = f = 120
d is the vertically opposite angle of b, so d = b = 120
f = b and b = d, so f = d, whatever the size of f
the slip: d and f share no arm, so they are not a linear pair and 180 - 120 = 60 is wrong
video_script.design: One figure for the whole video: two parallel lines, a transversal, eight angles a to h. A first arrow goes from f to b, a second arrow from b to d, in one colour for the size that is kept.

beats.on_screen: title card From your book; parallel lines l and m with a transversal t; eight angles a to h; f is 120°; d is across the transversal from f, between the lines

marks.scene: the title card From your book arrives
marks.lines: the parallel lines l and m and the transversal t are drawn with eight angles
marks.ask: d is highlighted with a question mark

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book about two parallel lines.
<bookmark mark='lines'/>A transversal t cuts the lines l and m, and makes eight angles.
<bookmark mark='given'/>The angle f is one hundred and twenty degrees.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>The angle d is across the transversal from f, between the lines. How big is d?

beats.on_screen: the figure stays on the board with a question mark on d

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: the figure; the pair f and b in the same corner glows; the pair b and d facing each other glows; d and f are joined by a curved arrow across t; the words alternate angle are written

marks.corr: f and b glow in one colour, in the same corner at the two crossings
marks.vert: b and d glow in another colour, facing each other at one crossing
marks.alt: d is on the other side of t from f, between the lines, and a curved arrow joins d and f

beats.colours: the corresponding pair and the vertically opposite pair have two colours
narration: <bookmark mark='corr'/>Corresponding angles sit in the same corner, and for parallel lines they are equal.
<bookmark mark='vert'/>Vertically opposite angles face each other, and they are equal as well.
<bookmark mark='alt'/>The angle d is between the lines, on the other side of t from f. It is called the alternate angle of f.

beats.on_screen: Given: l is parallel to m, t is a transversal, f = 120°

marks.given: the given line is written on the board

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, l and m are parallel, and t is a transversal.
The angle f is one hundred and twenty degrees.

beats.on_screen: To find: the alternate angle d

marks.find: the word d is written under the given

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the alternate angle d.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: b is the corresponding angle of f, so b = f = 120°

marks.move: an arrow goes from f to b

narration: <bookmark mark='move'/>Step one, go from f to its corresponding angle b.
<bookmark mark='size'/>The lines are parallel, so corresponding angles are equal, and b is one hundred and twenty degrees.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: d is the vertically opposite angle of b, so d = b

marks.move: a second arrow goes from b to d
marks.equal: an equals sign joins d and b

narration: <bookmark mark='move'/>Step two, go from b to its vertically opposite angle d.
<bookmark mark='equal'/>Vertically opposite angles are equal, so d is as big as b.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: f = b and b = d, so f = d, whatever the size of f

marks.chain: the two equalities join into one chain from f to d

narration: <bookmark mark='chain'/>Step three, join the two moves. The angle f equals b, and b equals d, so f equals d.
Neither move depends on how big f is.

beats.on_screen: Answer: d = 120°, so alternate angles of parallel lines are equal

marks.ans: the answer is boxed on the board

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Each move keeps the size the same.
The alternate angle d is one hundred and twenty degrees, so alternate angles of parallel lines are equal.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the board
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's doubt: d = 60° is shown, then struck out; d and f have no shared arm; the chain f, b, d lights up

marks.fix: the bubble is struck out and the missing shared arm is shown
marks.right: the chain from f to d lights up

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks d is sixty, because Keeko takes d and f to be a linear pair.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>But d and f share no arm, so they are not neighbours on a straight line.
<bookmark mark='right'/>Alternate angles are equal, so d is one hundred and twenty degrees.
